content: The study compared the efficacy of anakinra versus standard of care (SOC) in patients with COVID-19 through a randomized controlled trial (RCT). 1. All-cause mortality: The analysis included 5 studies with a total of 1147 participants. The risk ratio (RR) for all-cause mortality was 0.93, with a 95% confidence interval (CI) of 0.58 to 1.50. This suggests no statistically significant difference in mortality between the anakinra group and the usual care group. 2. Discharged from hospital at day 28: Data from 4 studies involving 805 participants were analyzed. The risk ratio for being discharged from the hospital by day 28 was 1.05, with a 95% CI of 0.98 to 1.13. This indicates no significant difference in discharge rates between the two groups. 3. Time to hospital discharge: Two studies with 624 participants assessed the mean difference in time to hospital discharge. The mean difference was -4.64 days (95% CI: -12.88 to 3.61), suggesting that anakinra may reduce the time to discharge, but the result is not statistically significant. 4. Clinical improvement: One study with 342 participants reported a risk ratio of 1.00 (95% CI: 0.87 to 1.14), indicating no significant difference in clinical improvement between the anakinra and SOC groups. 5. ICU admission: One study with 71 participants reported a risk ratio of 0.57 (95% CI: 0.27 to 1.19). This suggests a potential reduction in ICU admissions with anakinra, but the result is not statistically significant. 6. Length of ICU stay: Two studies with 624 participants reported a mean difference of -7.45 days (95% CI: -14.47 to -0.42). This indicates that anakinra may significantly reduce the length of ICU stay compared to SOC. 7. Discharged from ICU at day 28: One study with 42 participants reported a risk ratio of 1.33 (95% CI: 1.00 to 1.78). This suggests a potential increase in the likelihood of ICU discharge by day 28 with anakinra, but the result is borderline significant. 8. Mechanical ventilation: Four studies with 805 participants reported a risk ratio of 0.60 (95% CI: 0.36 to 1.00). This suggests that anakinra may reduce the need for mechanical ventilation, with the result approaching statistical significance. 9. Non-invasive ventilation: One study with 67 participants reported results that were not estimable, indicating insufficient data to draw conclusions. 10. Serious adverse events: Four studies with 809 participants reported a risk ratio of 0.93 (95% CI: 0.70 to 1.24). This suggests no significant difference in the occurrence of serious adverse events between the anakinra and SOC groups. These findings were analyzed using Review Manager version 5.4.1.
